activities.description: Practice greeting routines — hello wave, hi-five — to build social etiquette.

activities.title: Toy In The Box
activities.description: Place a toy inside a box and let baby figure out how to get it out.

activities.title: Pull Action
activities.description: Attach a ribbon to a toy and show baby how to pull it to retrieve the toy.

activities.title: Object Finding Game
activities.description: Hide a favourite toy under one of several cloths for baby to search and find.

activities.title: Object Revealing
activities.description: Partially uncover different objects for baby to identify using context clues.

activities.title: Shake The Bottle
activities.description: Give baby a sealed bottle with beads inside to shake and hear, sparking curiosity.

activities.title: Playing Drums
activities.description: Let baby bang pots, drums, or surfaces with a soft stick to develop rhythm.

activities.title: Building Vocabulary L2
activities.description: Introduce two-word phrases alongside single words to grow baby's vocabulary.

activities.title: Shaping Things With Hands
activities.description: Give baby play dough or soft clay to squeeze, press, and shape.

activities.title: Creating Sounds
activities.description: Encourage baby to bang, shake, or blow objects to produce sounds creatively.

activities.title: Verbal Directions
activities.description: Give simple one-step instructions — "give me the ball" — and celebrate compliance.

activities.title: Fast & Slow Clapping
activities.description: Clap hands fast then slow to teach baby tempo and build listening skills.

activities.title: Finger Pick And Drop
activities.description: Practice picking up and deliberately dropping small safe objects into a container.

activities.title: Removing Rings
activities.description: Stack rings on a peg and let baby remove them to build fine motor skills.

activities.title: Getting The Toy
activities.description: Place a desired toy behind a barrier so baby must reason and reach around it.

activities.title: Counting Toes
activities.description: Count baby's toes aloud while touching each one to introduce number concepts.

activities.title: Goof Off
activities.description: Be silly together — funny faces, silly sounds — to build baby's sense of self and humour.

activities.title: Finding Sound Source
activities.description: Hide a sound-making toy and encourage baby to crawl toward and find it.

activities.title: Rotating Objects
activities.description: Show baby how to rotate and turn objects to see all sides, building spatial cognition.

activities.title: Crawling Long Distance
activities.description: Encourage baby to crawl across a larger open space to build endurance and confidence.

activities.title: Standing Up
activities.description: Practice pulling to standing from sitting using furniture for support.

activities.title: Walk With Help
activities.description: Hold baby's hands and walk forward together to prepare for independent steps.

activities.title: One Hand To Other
activities.description: Encourage baby to pass a small object from one hand to the other.

activities.title: Taking Out Things
activities.description: Fill a small box with safe objects for baby to take out one by one.

activities.title: Standing Foundation L3
activities.description: With minimal support, let baby stand briefly against furniture to build confidence.

activities.title: Join The Fun
activities.description: Let baby join a small group activity to experience cooperative social play.

activities.title: Tummy Time
activities.description: Place baby on tummy for short periods to strengthen neck and back muscles
activities.instructions: Place baby on tummy for 2-5 minutes, 2-3 times daily. Use colorful toys to encourage head lifting.

activities.title: High Contrast Cards
activities.description: Show black and white cards to stimulate visual development
activities.instructions: Hold cards 8-12 inches from baby's face. Move slowly to track eye movement.

activities.title: Singing & Rhymes
activities.description: Sing songs and recite nursery rhymes to develop language skills
activities.instructions: Sing simple songs, recite nursery rhymes. Use gestures and facial expressions.

activities.title: Reach & Grab
activities.description: Encourage baby to reach for and grasp objects
activities.instructions: Place toys just out of reach. Encourage baby to reach and grab.

activities.title: Peek-a-Boo
activities.description: Classic game to develop object permanence
activities.instructions: Hide your face behind hands or blanket, then reveal with "peek-a-boo!"

activities.title: Stacking Blocks
activities.description: Stack and knock down blocks to develop fine motor skills
activities.instructions: Show baby how to stack blocks. Let them explore and knock down.

activities.title: Reading Books
activities.description: Read picture books to develop language and attention
activities.instructions: Read colorful picture books. Point to pictures and name objects.

activities.title: Music & Movement
activities.description: Play music and encourage movement and dancing
activities.instructions: Play upbeat music. Dance with baby, clap hands, move to rhythm.

activities.title: Shape Sorter
activities.description: Match shapes to develop problem-solving skills
activities.instructions: Show baby how to match shapes. Encourage independent play.

activities.title: Pretend Play
activities.description: Encourage imaginative play with toys
activities.instructions: Engage in pretend play. Model actions like feeding dolls or driving cars.

activities.title: Learning Through Books
activities.description: Share simple picture books with your baby to introduce words, images, and the joy of reading together.
activities.instructions:
1. Choose a simple board book with bright pictures.
2. Sit comfortably with baby on your lap.
3. Point to each picture and name it clearly.
4. Use different voices and sounds to bring characters to life.
5. Let baby touch and turn pages with your guidance.
benefits: Introduces concepts like animals, colors, and shapes

activities.title: Three Objects
activities.description: Present three objects to baby, then hide one and ask baby to identify the missing item, building memory and reasoning.
materials_needed: Three small familiar toys or household objects
activities.instructions:
1. Place three familiar objects in front of baby.
2. Name each one and let baby touch them.
3. Hide one under a cloth while baby watches.
4. Ask "Which one is missing?"
5. Lift the cloth to reveal it, then repeat with a different object.

activities.title: Do Messy Painting
activities.description: Let baby explore paint with their hands and fingers, developing creativity and fine motor skills through sensory art.
activities.instructions:
1. Lay a large sheet of paper on a protected surface.
2. Put baby-safe, washable paint in small amounts on the paper.
3. Guide baby's hands into the paint and let them explore.
4. Encourage spreading, pressing, and patting motions.
5. Display the artwork and clean up together.

activities.title: Granularity
activities.description: Explore materials of different textures and grain sizes to develop tactile sensitivity and fine motor pinching skills.
activities.instructions:
1. Fill small containers with rice, sand, or oats.
2. Let baby touch, scoop, and pour between containers.
3. Show baby how to pinch and pick up small amounts.
4. Describe the textures: "rough", "smooth", "grainy".
5. Supervise closely to prevent mouthing.

activities.title: Stacking Rings
activities.description: Stack colorful rings onto a central peg to develop hand-eye coordination and understanding of size sequences.
activities.instructions:
1. Place the stacking ring toy on the floor in front of baby.
2. Show how to slide a ring onto the peg.
3. Hand baby a ring and guide their hand if needed.
4. Cheer when a ring is placed successfully.
5. Count rings together as you stack from largest to smallest.

activities.title: Messy Activity
activities.description: Provide a safe, supervised messy play experience using different textures to stimulate all the senses.
activities.instructions:
1. Set up a protected area with a mat or tray.
2. Offer materials like cooked pasta, oats, or shaving foam.
3. Encourage baby to touch, squeeze, and explore freely.
4. Name textures: "slippery", "soft", "bumpy".
5. Allow free exploration for 10–15 minutes then clean up together.

activities.title: Finger Pinching And Poking
activities.description: Practice pinching and poking soft materials to develop isolated finger movement and strength.
activities.instructions:
1. Prepare soft play dough or a foam mat.
2. Show baby how to poke with one finger.
3. Encourage baby to make holes by pushing fingers in.
4. Show pinching — squeezing between thumb and index finger.
5. Make it playful: pop bubbles, press buttons on toys.
benefits: Prepares fine motor skills for future tasks

activities.title: Find The Object
activities.description: Hide a toy partially or fully and encourage baby to search and find it, developing object permanence.
activities.instructions:
1. Show baby an interesting toy and let them hold it.
2. Slowly cover it with a small blanket while baby watches.
3. Say "Where did it go?" with a curious expression.
4. Wait for baby to reach and pull the blanket off.
5. Celebrate the discovery! Gradually hide the toy more completely.

activities.title: Finger Grasp
activities.description: Practice picking up small objects using a pincer or tripod grasp to develop fine motor precision.
materials_needed: Puffed cereal or soft small cubes
activities.instructions:
1. Place small, safe objects (puffed cereal, soft cubes) on a tray.
2. Demonstrate picking one up with two fingers.
3. Encourage baby to try picking them up independently.
4. Praise each attempt, successful or not.
5. Gradually reduce object size as skill improves.
benefits: Develops pincer grip essential for writing

activities.title: Stand Without Support
activities.description: Practice standing independently without holding onto anything, building core strength and balance.
activities.instructions:
1. Place baby on a soft mat in a clear space.
2. Help baby stand upright, then gently let go while staying close.
3. Cheer and encourage as baby holds the position.
4. Catch or support if baby starts to fall.
5. Repeat for short bursts of 5–10 seconds.

activities.title: Stand Up
activities.description: Practice pushing up from seated or crawling position to standing, strengthening legs and building independence.
materials_needed: Low coffee table or couch edge
activities.instructions:
1. Sit baby on the floor next to a low stable surface.
2. Place a toy on the surface to motivate reaching up.
3. Support baby's hips as they push to stand.
4. Reduce support gradually as strength improves.
5. Cheer every time baby reaches a full standing position.

activities.title: Yes & No L2
activities.description: Build understanding of yes/no responses through simple questions and clear positive or negative reactions.
activities.instructions:
1. Ask simple yes/no questions: "Do you want water?" "Is this a ball?".
2. Nod your head for yes and shake for no with each answer.
3. Wait for baby to respond with head movement or sound.
4. Praise correct responses enthusiastically.
5. Use real situations — snack time, toy choices — for practice.

activities.title: Tactical Grip
activities.description: Practice grasping objects of different shapes and weights to develop a purposeful, coordinated grip.
activities.instructions:
1. Offer baby objects of varying shapes: round ball, flat block, cylinder.
2. Encourage baby to pick up and hold each one.
3. Show how to transfer objects from one hand to the other.
4. Offer slightly heavier objects as skills improve.
5. Cheer each successful grip and transfer.
benefits: Builds dexterity for future tool use

activities.title: Anticipating Events 2
activities.description: Build anticipation by doing familiar routines with a pause before the exciting moment, developing prediction skills.
activities.instructions:
1. Start a familiar playful routine, like "Round and Round the Garden".
2. Slow down before the exciting climax and wait.
3. Watch as baby shows anticipation — lean forward, giggle, hold breath.
4. Complete the action and celebrate together.
5. Repeat with other familiar games and songs.

activities.title: Image Vs Live Objects
activities.description: Compare pictures in books or photos with real objects to help baby connect images to the real world.
activities.instructions:
1. Hold up a real object, such as a ball or cup.
2. Find a picture of the same object in a book or on a card.
3. Place them side by side and say the name of each.
4. Encourage baby to touch both and look back and forth.
5. Repeat with different objects and their pictures.
benefits: Builds vocabulary by connecting words to images

activities.title: Peekaboo Bath
activities.description: A fun water-based peekaboo game that turns bath time into an exciting exploration experience.
activities.instructions:
1. Fill the bathtub with a comfortable water level.
2. Hold a small towel or washcloth over your face.
3. Say "Where is Mommy?" then pull it away saying "Peekaboo!"
4. Let baby grab the towel and try the same game.
5. Repeat with different objects floating in the water.

activities.title: Dada And Mama
activities.description: Encourage baby to say "dada" and "mama" by modeling these words in meaningful, positive contexts.
activities.instructions:
1. Point to yourself and say "Mama!" or "Dada!" with a big smile.
2. Point to the other parent and say their name.
3. Repeat the names frequently throughout the day.
4. Respond with excitement when baby makes similar sounds.
5. Use the words in context: "Where is Dada? Here is Dada!"
benefits: Builds understanding of people and names

activities.title: Gesture Communication
activities.description: Teach baby to use simple gestures like waving, pointing, and reaching to communicate needs and ideas.
activities.instructions:
1. Wave hello and goodbye every time you greet or part.
2. Point to objects and say their names clearly.
3. Reach out your arms asking for a hug and encourage baby to mimic.
4. Use "more" gesture (fingertips together) at mealtimes.
5. Respond enthusiastically whenever baby uses any gesture.
benefits: Reduces frustration by giving baby a voice

activities.title: Walking With Assistance L1
activities.description: Support baby's first walking steps by holding both hands and guiding their movement forward.
activities.instructions:
1. Stand or kneel behind baby on a clear, safe floor.
2. Hold both of baby's hands at shoulder height.
3. Gently encourage baby to step forward one foot at a time.
4. Move slowly, matching baby's pace.
5. Practice for a few minutes and gradually loosen support.

activities.title: Hugs And Kisses
activities.description: Teach baby the warmth of giving and receiving affection through gentle hugs and kisses with family.
activities.instructions:
1. Hold baby and give a warm hug while saying "Hug!".
2. Give a gentle kiss and say "Kiss!".
3. Encourage baby to lean in for a hug or pucker up.
4. Clap and praise when baby initiates affection.
5. Practice with different family members.

activities.title: Climbing Down A Step
activities.description: Practice safely descending a small step or ledge feet-first to build lower body strength and spatial awareness.
activities.instructions:
1. Find a single low step or use a foam block.
2. Show baby how to turn around and lower feet first.
3. Guide baby's body to turn, then support as feet touch down.
4. Say "feet first, down we go!" as you practice.
5. Praise each attempt and repeat until confident.
benefits: Builds leg and core muscle strength

activities.title: Turning The Pages
activities.description: Practice turning book pages to develop finger dexterity, bilateral coordination, and a love of books.
activities.instructions:
1. Sit with baby and open a board book.
2. Show how to grip and turn one page at a time.
3. Help baby's fingers grasp a page edge and turn it.
4. Celebrate each page turn with excitement.
5. Progress to thinner paper pages as skill develops.

activities.title: Playing With Siblings
activities.description: Encourage interaction between baby and older siblings through supervised play to build social awareness.
activities.instructions:
1. Create a safe shared play space.
2. Give each child an age-appropriate toy to explore together.
3. Model taking turns and sharing between siblings.
4. Narrate the interaction: "Look, your brother is rolling the ball to you!"
5. Praise gentle, kind behavior from both children.

activities.title: Climbing Up A Step
activities.description: Practice stepping up onto a low platform or step to develop leg strength, balance, and body confidence.
activities.instructions:
1. Place a single low step or foam block in a clear area.
2. Hold baby's hands and encourage stepping up one foot at a time.
3. Cheer with each successful step.
4. Practice stepping down the same way.
5. Allow independent attempts with close supervision.

activities.title: Learn To Sit Down
activities.description: Practice controlled sitting down from a standing position, building core strength and body control.
activities.instructions:
1. Stand baby upright holding their hands.
2. Slowly bend knees, guiding baby into a squat and then to seated.
3. Say "Down we go, sit!" as you lower them.
4. Let baby try independently near a soft surface.
5. Repeat from different starting positions.
benefits: Prevents falls by practicing safe descent

activities.title: Head To Head
activities.description: A gentle bonding game where baby and caregiver gently touch foreheads, sharing closeness and warmth.
activities.instructions:
1. Sit facing baby at eye level.
2. Slowly lean in and gently touch foreheads together.
3. Say "Head to head!" in a warm, playful voice.
4. Hold for a moment, then lean back smiling.
5. Repeat and let baby lean in to initiate.

activities.title: Repeat Actions
activities.description: Imitate baby's sounds and actions to show that their expressions are valued, building self-worth and communication.
activities.instructions:
1. Observe baby making a sound, gesture, or facial expression.
2. Immediately mimic the same action back.
3. Pause and wait — baby may repeat it again.
4. Add a small variation and see if baby follows.
5. Keep it playful and celebrate the back-and-forth.

activities.title: Reading Book By Themselves
activities.description: Allow baby to independently explore a book, encouraging autonomy and a personal relationship with reading.
activities.instructions:
1. Give baby a durable board book they enjoy.
2. Sit nearby but let baby explore independently.
3. Observe which pages baby pauses on and engage about those.
4. Name pictures if baby looks to you for input.
5. Let baby turn pages at their own pace.

activities.title: Play With Dough
activities.description: Manipulate soft play dough by squeezing, rolling, and poking to develop creativity and fine motor skills.
materials_needed: Baby-safe play dough or homemade salt dough
activities.instructions:
1. Give baby a small ball of soft, safe play dough.
2. Show how to press, roll, and squeeze it.
3. Make simple shapes together — ball, snake, flat pancake.
4. Press objects into the dough to make impressions.
5. Narrate the play: "You made a worm!"
benefits: Develops fine motor strength and dexterity

activities.title: Tasting Time
activities.description: Introduce a variety of safe food flavors and textures to expand palate and develop oral sensory processing.
activities.instructions:
1. Prepare small portions of different safe foods: sweet, sour, salty.
2. Offer each taste one at a time.
3. Watch baby's reaction and name the flavor.
4. Celebrate all reactions — even funny ones!
5. Never force — let baby lead the pace.

activities.title: Stretch The Feet
activities.description: Do gentle foot and ankle stretches to improve flexibility, circulation, and body awareness in baby's lower limbs.
activities.instructions:
1. Lay baby on their back on a soft mat.
2. Hold one foot gently and flex it forward and back.
3. Make gentle circles with the ankle.
4. Point and flex the toes playfully.
5. Repeat on the other foot and use a sing-song voice throughout.
benefits: Builds a positive relationship with physical touch

activities.title: Fluid Difference
activities.description: Pour and transfer water or other fluids between containers to experience cause-and-effect and build pouring skills.
activities.instructions:
1. Set up two containers of different sizes at the water table or bathtub.
2. Show baby how to pour water from one to the other.
3. Let baby try — embrace the spills!
4. Use language: "full", "empty", "pouring".
5. Try with slightly thicker fluids like watery oats.

activities.title: Sitting To Standing Position
activities.description: Practice transitioning from sitting on the floor to a standing position to build leg strength and coordination.
activities.instructions:
1. Have baby sit on the floor near a low stable surface.
2. Place a motivating toy on the surface.
3. Encourage baby to push up to standing to reach it.
4. Support baby's hips lightly if needed.
5. Practice 5–8 repetitions each session.
benefits: Prepares for walking and stair climbing

activities.title: Hold And Walk
activities.description: Walk while holding a stable object or furniture to build confidence and leg strength for independent walking.
activities.instructions:
1. Position baby next to a low sofa, table, or push toy.
2. Encourage baby to hold on and take steps sideways.
3. Slowly move your hands away, guiding less each time.
4. Place a motivating toy a few steps away.
5. Celebrate each step taken.

activities.title: Similar And Different
activities.description: Compare pairs of objects that are similar or different to develop early categorization and reasoning skills.
materials_needed: Pairs of matching and non-matching toys
activities.instructions:
1. Choose pairs of objects — one same (two balls) and one different (ball and block).
2. Hold up a same pair and say "Same!"
3. Hold up a different pair and say "Different!"
4. Let baby handle both and observe their exploration.
5. Ask "Are these the same?" and respond to baby's cues.
benefits: Introduces concepts of same and different

activities.title: Sound Vibrations
activities.description: Explore how sound vibrations can be felt as well as heard by touching musical instruments and vibrating surfaces.
activities.instructions:
1. Play a drum or tap a surface and let baby feel the vibrations.
2. Hold baby's hand on the drum as you tap.
3. Turn on music and place baby's hand on the speaker (safe distance).
4. Hum and let baby feel your throat vibrate.
5. Try different pitches and ask "Can you feel it?"
benefits: Stimulates curiosity about the physical world

activities.title: Stand And Play
activities.description: Play with toys while standing to challenge balance and develop the ability to use hands while standing upright.
activities.instructions:
1. Position toys on a table or surface at baby's standing height.
2. Help baby stand holding the surface.
3. Encourage reaching for and manipulating the toys.
4. Gradually step back as baby gains confidence.
5. Celebrate each moment of independent standing play.

activities.title: Weather Talk
activities.description: Discuss daily weather during outdoor time to build vocabulary related to the natural environment.
activities.instructions:
1. Step outside or look out a window each day.
2. Describe the weather simply: "It's sunny and warm today."
3. Point to clouds, sun, rain, or wind in action.
4. Use expressive language: "The wind is blowing our hair!"
5. Connect clothing choices to weather: "We wear coats when it's cold."

activities.title: Crawl Through Tunnel
activities.description: Crawl through a fabric tunnel, stimulating imagination, spatial awareness, and whole-body coordination.
activities.instructions:
1. Set up a collapsible fabric tunnel on the floor.
2. Show baby the opening and crawl through yourself first.
3. Place a toy inside or at the other end for motivation.
4. Cheer as baby enters and crawls through.
5. Make sounds and stories: "Going through the cave!"

activities.title: Stand And Lift
activities.description: Stand and lift one foot or a toy off the ground to develop single-leg balance and core stability.
activities.instructions:
1. Help baby stand near a stable support surface.
2. Hold a toy slightly to the side to encourage weight shifting.
3. Gently lift baby's foot slightly off the ground.
4. Hold for 2–3 seconds then place foot down.
5. Switch sides and repeat several times.
benefits: Prepares for stair climbing and running

activities.title: Walking With Support
activities.description: Use a push toy or walker for supported independent walking, building leg strength and walking rhythm.
activities.instructions:
1. Place a stable push toy on a clear, flat floor.
2. Position baby behind it and encourage pushing forward.
3. Walk alongside for safety, offering minimal support.
4. Guide direction gently when needed.
5. Increase distance gradually as confidence grows.

activities.title: Learn To Walk
activities.description: Take first independent steps toward a caregiver or between two adults, building walking confidence.
activities.instructions:
1. Sit a short distance from baby (1–2 steps).
2. Hold out your hands and call baby to come to you.
3. As baby takes a step, lean forward encouragingly.
4. Catch baby in a big celebratory hug.
5. Gradually increase distance as confidence grows.

activities.title: Walking With Assistance L2
activities.description: Walk with only one-hand support from a caregiver, preparing for fully independent walking.
activities.instructions:
1. Hold one of baby's hands at a comfortable height.
2. Walk together slowly across the room.
3. Gradually loosen your grip to minimal fingertip contact.
4. Place motivating toys at the destination.
5. Celebrate each stretch of independent steps.

activities.title: Curious In Park
activities.description: Explore a park environment using all senses — touch leaves, smell flowers, hear birds — for rich sensory learning.
materials_needed: Access to a park or garden
activities.instructions:
1. Take baby to a park or garden.
2. Let baby touch grass, leaves, tree bark, and soil.
3. Smell flowers and point out different scents.
4. Listen to birds and wind, naming the sounds.
5. Describe everything using rich sensory language.

activities.title: Sing To Baby
activities.description: Sing simple songs and nursery rhymes to baby to develop language comprehension, rhythm, and emotional bonding.
activities.instructions:
1. Choose 2–3 short familiar songs or rhymes.
2. Sing face-to-face with baby at a slow, clear pace.
3. Use hand gestures and facial expressions.
4. Repeat the same songs often so baby recognizes them.
5. Pause in familiar spots and wait for baby to fill in.

activities.title: Tickling Spider
activities.description: Use your fingers to "walk like a spider" across baby's tummy and arms, sparking imagination and delight.
activities.instructions:
1. Start with fingers on baby's leg saying "Here comes the spider!"
2. Walk your fingers slowly up toward baby's tummy.
3. At the tummy, do a fun tickle or wiggle.
4. Add dramatic suspense with pauses.
5. Let baby try to "stop" the spider with their hands.

activities.title: Fishing In A Bathtub
activities.description: Scoop and catch floating toys from the bathtub using a small net or cup, building fine motor and coordination skills.
activities.instructions:
1. Float several bath toys in the tub.
2. Give baby a small cup or mesh scooper.
3. Show how to scoop toys out of the water.
4. Name each toy as it is caught.
5. Encourage baby to try independently and celebrate successes.
benefits: Introduces tool use for fine motor tasks

activities.title: Visiting People
activities.description: Practice greeting and interacting politely with familiar people outside the home to build social confidence.
activities.instructions:
1. Plan a visit to familiar relatives or friends.
2. Model polite greetings: wave, say "Hello!"
3. Encourage baby to greet others the same way.
4. Narrate social situations: "We are saying hello to Grandma."
5. Keep visits short and positive.
benefits: Builds social confidence in new environments

activities.title: Body Part
activities.description: Identify and name major body parts through a fun interactive game, building vocabulary and body awareness.
activities.instructions:
1. Sit with baby facing you or use a mirror.
2. Touch your own nose and say "Nose!"
3. Then touch baby's nose saying "Your nose!"
4. Ask "Where is your nose?" and guide baby's hand.
5. Work through eyes, ears, mouth, hands, and tummy.

activities.title: Throwing Ball L1
activities.description: Practice underhand tossing of a soft ball to develop arm coordination, grip, and release skills.
activities.instructions:
1. Sit facing baby about one meter apart.
2. Hold a soft ball and show an underarm toss toward baby.
3. Encourage baby to throw the ball back to you.
4. Gradually increase distance as skill improves.
5. Count throws and celebrate each successful toss.

activities.title: Standing On Soft Surface
activities.description: Practice standing on an unstable soft surface like a foam mat to challenge and develop balance reactions.
activities.instructions:
1. Place a soft foam mat or folded blanket on the floor.
2. Help baby stand on the soft surface.
3. Stay close and hold hands lightly.
4. Let baby feel the slight wobble and self-correct.
5. Increase duration as balance improves.
benefits: Prepares for walking on varied surfaces

activities.title: Empty A Container
activities.description: Practice removing objects from a container one by one to develop reach, grasp, and release skills.
activities.instructions:
1. Fill a small basket or box with soft toys or blocks.
2. Show baby how to reach in and take one item out.
3. Encourage baby to empty the container completely.
4. Name each object as it comes out.
5. Put them all back in and repeat.

activities.title: Open & Close
activities.description: Practice opening and closing containers, books, and boxes to develop hand control, problem-solving, and cause-and-effect.
activities.instructions:
1. Gather containers with simple lids, boxes, and books.
2. Show opening and closing each one slowly.
3. Let baby try to open and close independently.
4. Narrate: "Open! Now close it."
5. Hide a surprise inside for extra motivation.
benefits: Develops wrist rotation and hand control

activities.title: Different Aromas 2
activities.description: Explore a variety of distinct scents to develop the olfactory sense and expand sensory vocabulary.
activities.instructions:
1. Prepare 3–4 safe scents: citrus peel, lavender, vanilla, mint.
2. Present one scent at a time in a small container.
3. Waft it gently under baby's nose.
4. Name the smell: "That's lemon! It smells fresh."
5. Watch for and describe baby's reactions.

activities.title: Sponge Play
activities.description: Squeeze and release a sponge in water to explore absorption, cause-and-effect, and basic science concepts.
activities.instructions:
1. Fill a shallow tray with water.
2. Give baby a sponge and demonstrate squeezing.
3. Show how the sponge absorbs water and releases it.
4. Let baby squeeze and explore freely.
5. Narrate: "It's full of water! Squeeze it out!"

activities.title: Memory Training
activities.description: Use simple matching or hiding games to exercise working memory and sustained attention.
activities.instructions:
1. Show two matching cards or objects, then shuffle them face down.
2. Let baby turn one over and find its match.
3. Keep the game to 2–3 pairs for this age.
4. Narrate: "You found the duck! Can you find the other one?"
5. Celebrate each match found.

activities.title: Who Is In The Mirror
activities.description: Explore the mirror to discover self-recognition, building self-awareness and visual attention skills.
activities.instructions:
1. Sit with baby in front of a mirror at a comfortable height.
2. Point to baby's reflection: "Who is that?"
3. Point to your own reflection: "That's Mama!"
4. Play with making funny faces together.
5. Place a sticker on baby's nose and see if they touch it or the reflection.

activities.title: Fun With Paper
activities.description: Explore paper by tearing, crumpling, and folding to discover textures, sounds, and creative possibilities.
activities.instructions:
1. Provide large sheets of safe, non-toxic paper.
2. Let baby crumple it and listen to the crinkling sound.
3. Tear pieces together — guide baby's hands.
4. Fold simple shapes and name them.
5. Wrap a toy in paper and let baby "unwrap" it.
benefits: Builds fine motor strength through tearing

activities.title: Walking With Objects
activities.description: Walk around while holding or carrying an object, developing balance and coordination during functional movement.
activities.instructions:
1. Give baby a toy to carry in one or both hands.
2. Set a destination — a basket or another room.
3. Encourage baby to walk to the destination without dropping the toy.
4. Celebrate successful delivery.
5. Vary objects: light, slightly heavier, different shapes.
benefits: Develops walking balance with added challenge
Builds bilateral hand and arm control

activities.title: Taking Objects
activities.description: Practice reaching, grasping, and transporting objects from one location to another to build functional movement.
activities.instructions:
1. Place objects in one container across the room from an empty one.
2. Encourage baby to carry objects from full to empty container.
3. Show how to carry one item at a time, walking across.
4. Narrate: "Bring it here!" and celebrate arrivals.
5. Vary the weight and size of objects.

activities.title: Moving Large Objects
activities.description: Push, pull, or carry slightly large objects to develop whole-body strength and spatial planning.
activities.instructions:
1. Place a large soft toy, box, or cushion on the floor.
2. Show baby how to push it across the room.
3. Encourage pulling it with both hands.
4. Make it a game: "Move it to the other side!"
5. Use language: "Push! Pull! Heavy! Light!"
benefits: Introduces concepts of heavy and light

activities.title: Familiarize With Family
activities.description: Look at family photos and meet relatives to strengthen baby's sense of belonging and family identity.
activities.instructions:
1. Gather photos of family members.
2. Point to each photo and name the person warmly.
3. Visit or video call relatives when possible.
4. Create a simple family photo book for baby.
5. Revisit the photos regularly, letting baby point to familiar faces.
benefits: Builds vocabulary of family member names

activities.title: Motion And Direction
activities.description: Explore objects moving in different directions — toward, away, up, down — to build spatial and directional understanding.
activities.instructions:
1. Roll a ball toward baby and away from them.
2. Lift toys up high and bring them down low.
3. Swing a toy left and right.
4. Narrate each movement: "Up! Down! Coming toward you!"
5. Let baby try moving toys in different directions.

activities.title: Give And Take
activities.description: Practice giving and taking objects back and forth to develop understanding of instructions and turn-taking.
activities.instructions:
1. Hold out your hand and say "Give me the ball."
2. Offer the ball back saying "Here you go, your turn."
3. Praise each exchange enthusiastically.
4. Use different objects to generalize the skill.
5. Introduce "please" and "thank you" modeling.
benefits: Develops receptive language for simple commands

activities.title: Object Identification
activities.description: Point to and name everyday objects to rapidly expand baby's receptive and expressive vocabulary.
activities.instructions:
1. Walk through different rooms together.
2. Point to objects and name them clearly: "Chair! Window! Cup!"
3. Ask "Where is the cup?" and guide baby to point.
4. Celebrate correct pointing enthusiastically.
5. Revisit the same objects daily to reinforce learning.

activities.title: Posture Words
activities.description: Demonstrate and label body postures like sitting, standing, lying, and crouching to build vocabulary and body awareness.
activities.instructions:
1. Demonstrate a posture: sit on the floor.
2. Say clearly: "Sitting!" then move to standing: "Standing!"
3. Lie down: "Lying down!" Crouch: "Crouching!"
4. Ask baby to do each: "Can you sit?"
5. Use these words throughout the day in context.
benefits: Develops receptive language for positional words

activities.title: Hide And Seek
activities.description: Play a gentle hide-and-seek game to develop object permanence, spatial thinking, and shared joy.
materials_needed: None required (or cloth for peekaboo variation)
activities.instructions:
1. Hide your face behind your hands or a cloth.
2. Say "Where is Mommy?" then reveal yourself: "Here I am!"
3. Progress to hiding behind furniture — peek out so baby can find you.
4. Cheer when baby finds you.
5. Let baby "hide" and pretend to search dramatically.

activities.title: Web Basket
activities.description: Thread, weave, or push objects through the holes of a basket or net to develop problem-solving and fine motor skills.
activities.instructions:
1. Provide a wicker basket or mesh bag and small balls or toys.
2. Show how to push a ball through a hole and retrieve it.
3. Encourage baby to try pushing objects through the weave.
4. Try pulling string or ribbon through holes.
5. Narrate: "Push it through! Where did it go?"
benefits: Introduces concepts of through and inside

activities.title: Stacking And Falling
activities.description: Stack blocks together then knock them down to explore cause-and-effect, gravity, and basic physics.
activities.instructions:
1. Build a simple tower of 3–5 soft blocks.
2. Hand baby a block and guide them to place it on top.
3. Build the tower as tall as possible.
4. Knock it down with a big "Boom!" together.
5. Laugh and rebuild — let baby knock it down alone.
benefits: Teaches that destruction is part of learning and play

activities.title: Give The Lead
activities.description: Let baby take the lead during playtime, following their choices and actions to build confidence and autonomy.
activities.instructions:
1. Set out a selection of toys and materials.
2. Step back and let baby choose what to play with.
3. Follow baby's lead — join in whatever they select.
4. Narrate their choices: "You chose the blocks! Great choice!"
5. Avoid redirecting — let the play be theirs.

instructions: Feed on demand.

instructions: Feed on demand.

recipes.title: Rice Cereal Porridge

Stir to smooth consistency.
Serve warm.

Mash banana.
Mix together and blend until smooth.

stories.title: The Hungry Sparrow
stories.description: A little sparrow is hungry and finds a big red apple. She cannot carry it, so she comes up with a clever idea to eat it bite by bite.
stories.content:
On a warm sunny day, a little sparrow was flying high in the sky. "Chi chi chi!" she chirped happily. She was hungry and started searching for food. After a long flight, she finally found something! It was a big, red apple!

"Yum yum yum!" The sparrow said and flew for the apple. But when she reached closer, she found that the apple was too big for her. The little sparrow tried to pick the apple up but she couldn't.

The little sparrow became sad. Then, she got an idea! She started pecking at the apple. "Peck peck peck," she went and began to eat small bites of the tasty red apple. "Nom nom nom," she pecked on. Soon, her tummy was full and the sparrow was happy. She said "Yay yay yay" and flew away.
stories.author: Fatema Arsiwala

stories.title: Ira's Hat
stories.description: A strong wind blows Ira's favourite hat away. A kind parrot comes to the rescue and returns the hat safely.
stories.content:
One fine morning, a little girl named Ira was walking down the road. She wore a blue dress and a beautiful white hat with red flowers. Suddenly, a strong wind blew and took Ira's hat away with it.

Ira ran after the hat, trying to catch it as it went on and on. But the wind was too fast and Ira couldn't reach her hat. So she called for help and said, "Help! Help!"

A parrot heard Ira and looked below to find the little girl running after her hat. He quickly flew to the hat and caught it in his strong beak. He gave the hat back to Ira. "Thank you, dear parrot!" said Ira happily. "Welcome!" said the parrot and flew away in the sky.
stories.author: Fatema Arsiwala

stories.title: Baby's Night Adventure
stories.description: Baby Coco cannot sleep and wishes to play. The moon and stars come to take her on a magical night adventure.
stories.content:
It was night time and mama had put baby Coco to bed. She kissed her on the cheek and then left the room.

Oh but baby Coco wasn't sleepy. She wanted to play. But mama was gone. So how would she play now?

Baby Coco giggled and looked outside the window. She saw the moon and so many stars, smiling down at her. "I want to play!" she told them.

A big star came flying down to baby Coco's room. Baby Coco sat on it and up she went into the sky with the twinkling star. "Whoosh!" went the star in the sky and baby Coco laughed.

Up in the sky, baby Coco jumped from one star to another saying "Weee!" Then she went to the tiny stars and started dancing with them. All night baby Coco played with the moon and the stars. Together, they had a lot of fun.

When finally she was tired, she wanted to sleep. "Come baby Coco. Sleep on me." The moon invited her. Baby Coco happily agreed. The moon rocked her lightly and sang her a gentle lullaby. When she fell asleep, it gently took her down and put baby Coco back into her bed.

Baby Coco smiled as she slept sweetly.
stories.author: Fatema Arsiwala

stories.title: The Red Shiny Ball
stories.description: Bobo the red ball plays with animal friends all day long, but gets dirty. Bobo finds a clever way to clean up.
stories.content:
Bobo was a big, red, shiny ball. It was a fun ball and loved to play. All-day it went around the garden to play with its friends. The dogs would toss Bobo high into the sky and then run after it when it fell down. The cats would cradle Bobo and say "meow meow" as they played with it. All the birds in the sky would peck at it playfully and Bobo would laugh.

But as the day ended, Bobo became dirty because of all the playing. Bobo was sad and wanted to clean itself. But how would it do that? Bobo thought on and on when it finally had an idea. It quickly rolled over to the lake nearby.

"Plash plash plash!" Went Bobo as it jumped into the lake. It started jumping happily in the water, cleaning all the mud from itself. When Bobo was done, it was shiny and clean again. Bobo was pleased and came out of the water. "I'll be back tomorrow!" it said to all animals and birds and then went home.
stories.author: Fatema Arsiwala

stories.title: Debbie's Ball
stories.description: Debbie the baby elephant loses her favourite red ball in the forest. Mama elephant shows her love by finding it.
stories.content:
On a nice summer day in the forest, Debbie the baby elephant was playing with her red ball. The ball was big and shiny and Debbie loved playing with it. With her long trunk, she threw the ball high in the sky and then caught it when it came down. But once, she threw the ball too high and too far. Far and far went the ball and then it was gone!

"Oh no!" cried Debbie. She searched for the ball everywhere but couldn't find it. Crying, she went back home and told Mama what had happened. "It's okay, little Debbie." cooed mama elephant but Debbie was still sad. All-day, she sat on her bed, sobbing for her dear red ball.

When night came, someone knocked on Debbie's door. Debbie opened the door to see her red ball flying there! "Yayy!" she said and picked up the ball. Mama elephant had gone to the forest and found her ball.

"Thank you so much, mama!" said Debbie happily. "Welcome, sweet Debbie." replied mama elephant and together they started playing with the shiny red ball.
stories.author: Fatema Arsiwala

stories.title: Baby Hana's Pet
stories.description: Baby Hana and her spotty dog Puff love to play together. One day Puff goes missing and Hana searches everywhere.
stories.content:
Baby Hana had a pet. It was a dog named Puff. He was white in color with small black spots on his body. It had two big blue eyes and a tiny black nose. His tongue was long and pink in color.

Puff loved running and playing all day long. Baby Hana enjoyed it too. They would play with their red shiny ball and the yellow choo-choo train.

But one day, baby Hana could not find Puff. She looked for him everywhere.

She looked over the bed and then under it. She searched for him inside the cupboards and all the rooms. She even asked mama but Puff was nowhere to be found.

"Where is little Puff?" wondered baby Hana.

"Puff! Puff!" called baby Hana loudly. And soon she heard Puff call back saying, "Woof! Woof!"
stories.author: Fatema Arsiwala

stories.title: The Blue Car and the Puddle
stories.description: Bub the blue car drives through a muddy puddle and needs help to get clean. Her friend Piffy the pink car saves the day.
stories.content:
On a bright sunny day, Bub the blue car was driving on the road. It was warm and Bub was enjoying the drive. "Vroom vroom vroom," drove Bub happily as she passed trees, animals, and birds.

All was well until Bub's wheels drove over a big puddle. The puddle splashed loudly and the dirty water got all over Bub's blue body. Oh no! Bub the blue car was so muddy. Now how would she clean herself?

Bub started to think and had an idea. She could go to her friend Piffy the pink car's house. She would help her. Bub rushed to Piffy's house and honked her horn loudly. Piffy the pink car heard and came out. She saw that Bub needed help and happily agreed. Piffy brought a big water pipe and sprayed it on Bub. "Splash Splash!" went the water and the dirty mud water washed away.

Bub thanked Piffy for her help and asked her if she would like to drive with her. "Yes!" said Piffy and together they drove away.
stories.author: Fatema Arsiwala

stories.title: The Sly Lion
stories.description: An aging lion uses a clever trick to catch deer. But the deer learn a valuable lesson about being careful.
stories.content:
In a big forest in South Africa lived many animals. In this forest, lived a big, strong lion. Every day, the lion would go out of his den and hunt and kill many deers. The deers were very scared of the lion.

But as the years passed, the lion grew older and weaker. And so he was not able to catch a lot of deers anymore. One day, he wasn't able to catch a single deer and was very hungry. So he decided to play a trick. He lay on his back and did not move at all.

A deer saw him and thought that the lion was dead. She happily ran to her friends and said, "The lion is dead! The lion is dead! Let us dance and play!"

The herd of deer was very happy to hear that the lion was dead. All of them started to dance and play around the lion. The lion continued to act dead and did not move at all.

After a while, one of the deers jumped onto the lion thinking it was safe. As soon as the deer came close enough, the lion grabbed it quickly. The other deer ran away in fear.

The lion smiled. His trick had worked! But the wise old owl watching from a tree called out to the other deer: "Always check twice before you trust, little ones. Safety must be earned, not assumed."
stories.author: Aesha Jhaveri

stories.title: The Brave Little Bunny
stories.description: A tiny bunny learns that courage means trying even when you are scared.
stories.content: Once upon a time, in a meadow full of clover, lived a tiny bunny named Biscuit. Biscuit had the softest white fur and the longest ears, but he was afraid of almost everything — the rustling leaves, the buzzing bees, even his own shadow. One afternoon his friend Daisy the duckling got stuck in the middle of the pond. Biscuit took a deep breath. "I am scared," he admitted, "but Daisy needs me." He hopped to the edge, found a long stick, and stretched it out until Daisy grabbed on. When she waddled safely to shore, she hugged him tight. "You were so brave!" she said. Biscuit smiled. "I was scared AND brave at the same time." And from that day on, he knew that those two things could live in his heart together.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: The Friendly Farm Animals
stories.description: Every animal on the farm has a special job and a special sound.
stories.content: Good morning! The sun is rising over Sunny Hill Farm, and all the animals are waking up. Moo! says the big brown cow as she stretches her legs. Oink oink! says the little pink pig rolling in the cool mud. Baa baa! say the fluffy white sheep nibbling the green grass. Cluck cluck! say the busy hens finding their breakfast seeds. And right at the top of the barn, the rooster crows cock-a-doodle-doo! to tell everyone the day has begun. Each animal has a job: the cow gives warm milk, the hens give fresh eggs, the sheep give soft wool, and the pig digs the garden with his snout. At the end of the day they all snuggle up together and whisper their sounds softly until they fall asleep. Moo… oink… baa… cluck… goodnight, farm.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: Goodnight Garden
stories.description: A soothing journey through a sleepy garden as everything settles down for the night.
stories.content: The sky is turning pink and purple and the garden is getting ready for sleep. The big sunflower slowly closes her golden petals and bows her head. The butterflies tuck their wings together and rest on the leaves. The little ladybirds find a cosy rosebud and crawl inside. The bees fly back to their hive and hum a quiet goodnight song. The crickets begin their gentle chirp chirp chirp. Even the stream slows down, its water barely whispering over the pebbles. A firefly blinks hello to the first star. The moon floats up and spreads a silver blanket over everything. Close your eyes, little one. The garden is sleeping, and it is time for you to sleep too.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: The Magic Paintbrush
stories.description: A child discovers a paintbrush that brings every picture to life.
stories.content: Lily found an old wooden paintbrush in her grandmother's attic. It had a golden tip and felt warm in her hand. She dipped it in blue paint and drew a puddle — and real water appeared on the floor! She drew a butterfly — and it fluttered right off the paper! Lily painted a sad cloud and gave it a rainbow, and the cloud started to smile. She painted a lonely tree and added a bird's nest, and a small bird flew in and began to sing. When evening came, she painted a soft pillow and a starry sky. "Is the magic in the brush?" she asked her grandmother. Grandma winked. "The magic was always in your imagination, little one. The brush just helped it out."
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: Grandma's Big Hugs
stories.description: A visit to grandma's house is full of love, cookies, and stories.
stories.content: Every Saturday morning, little Sam woke up to the smell of something wonderful. "Grandma day!" he shouted and jumped out of bed. Grandma lived just down the lane in a yellow house with a red door. When Sam knocked, the door swung open and two big arms scooped him right up. Grandma smelled like warm cookies and lavender. She always had the softest cardigan and the best stories. They baked oat biscuits together, and Sam got to stir the dough three times and make a wish each time. Then they sat by the window and Grandma told him about when his mum was a little girl, just like him. On the way home Sam held Grandma's hand and thought that the world was a very good place when you had someone who gave such big hugs.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: The Little Seed's Journey
stories.description: Follow a tiny seed from the soil all the way to a blooming flower.
stories.content: Deep inside the dark, warm soil, a tiny seed was sleeping. Rain came drip drip drip and the seed began to wake up. It pushed a small white root down and a green shoot up, up, up toward the light. The shoot peeked out of the ground and felt the sunshine for the very first time. "Hello, world!" it whispered. Days passed. The shoot grew taller and grew leaves that spread wide to catch the sun. A worm helped loosen the soil around its roots. A bee visited and dusted it with golden pollen. Then one bright morning, a bud appeared, tight and round. Slowly, slowly it opened — petal by petal — into a beautiful yellow flower. The seed had become something wonderful. And inside the flower, new seeds were already forming, ready to begin their own great journey.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: The Sharing Starfish
stories.description: A starfish with five arms learns that giving to others fills your heart.
stories.content: On a warm coral reef lived a starfish named Stella who had five bright orange arms. One day she found a pile of beautiful shells on the sea floor. She counted them — five shells, one for each arm! She was about to take them all when she saw her friend the crab looking sadly at the pile. "I was looking for a shell too," said the crab. Stella thought for a moment, then gave one shell away. Then a small fish swam by with a worried face — it needed a shell for its home. Stella gave another. Soon a sea snail, a little lobster, and a tiny shrimp had each received a shell. Stella looked at her one remaining shell and smiled. Her reef was now full of happy friends waving thank-you to her, and her heart felt five times bigger than before.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
stories.description: A curious toddler asks big questions and discovers that wondering is wonderful.
stories.content: Every morning, Zoe would press her nose against the window and ask a question. "Why is the sky blue?" she asked one Tuesday. Papa scratched his head and said the sunlight dances with tiny bits of air and blue bounces the most. Zoe thought about that. On Wednesday she asked, "Why do birds sing?" Mama smiled and said birds talk to each other in song, saying good morning and I am here and I love this tree. Zoe liked that. On Thursday she asked, "Why do I yawn?" Big sister said because your body is telling your brain it is time to rest. Zoe yawned right then and there. On Friday she asked, "Why is asking questions so fun?" No one answered for a long moment. Then they all said together: "Because questions are how we find out wonderful things."
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: Young Albert and the Compass
stories.description: Inspired by Albert Einstein's childhood, a boy is amazed by a magnetic compass.
stories.content: When Albert was five years old and sick in bed, his father brought him a small gift — a compass. Albert turned it this way and that way, but no matter which direction he pointed it, the needle always swung back to face north. He could not see anything touching the needle. He could not hear anything pulling it. Yet it always, always pointed north. "There is something invisible making it move," he whispered. He could not sleep that night for thinking about it. What hidden force reached through empty space and touched that little needle? He did not know the answer yet. But that tiny compass planted a seed of wonder in young Albert's mind — a wonder that would one day change everything we knew about the universe.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: Tidying Up With Teddy
stories.description: A child and their teddy bear make a game out of putting toys away.
stories.content: When the sun went down and dinnertime was over, Mia's room was a wonderful disaster. Blocks here, books there, puzzle pieces everywhere. "Time to tidy," said Mum. Mia looked at the mess. It felt very big. Then she had an idea. She picked up her teddy bear Tom and gave him a job. "Tom, you are in charge of the blocks," she said in her most serious voice. She walked Tom's little paws over each block and dropped them one by one into the basket. Clunk, clunk, clunk! Ten points! Then she raced the puzzle pieces back to their box. Then she lined the books up like a tiny colourful parade. When everything was done, Mia looked around at her tidy room. "We did it, Tom," she said. Tom's button eyes seemed to sparkle with pride.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: Luna's Bedtime Routine
stories.description: A little girl follows her cosy bedtime steps and feels safe and sleepy.
stories.content: Every evening when the stars began to appear, Luna started her bedtime routine. First she had a warm bath with her yellow duck who splashed and squeaked. Then she put on her softest pyjamas — the ones with the little moons on them. She brushed her teeth up and down, round and round, until they were sparkly clean. Then she chose one book from her shelf — tonight it was the one about the bear who found honey. After the story she had a big glass of water and gave everyone a goodnight hug: Mum, Dad, and her toy rabbit Pip. She climbed into bed, and Mum tucked the blanket snug around her feet. The nightlight glowed a soft golden colour. Luna closed her eyes. The routine was like a path of little stepping stones leading her gently all the way to sleep.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: The Curious Caterpillar
stories.description: A caterpillar questions everything and discovers the wonder of change.
stories.content: A tiny green caterpillar named Cleo munched her way along a leaf and asked questions with every bite. "Why are leaves green?" Munch. "What is that yellow thing up in the sky?" Munch. "Where does the wind come from?" Munch munch. One day she felt very sleepy and wrapped herself in a soft silky blanket she made herself. She slept and slept and dreamed and wondered. When she woke up and pushed her way out into the sunlight, she stretched — and found she had wings! Brilliant, jewelled, trembling wings that caught the light like tiny stained-glass windows. She flew up for the very first time and looked down at the leaf where she used to munch. Everything looked different from up here. "New questions!" she laughed, and flew off to find the answers.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: Dragon's First Day
stories.description: A young dragon is nervous about starting dragon school and makes a surprising friend.
stories.content: Drake the dragon woke up on the first day of Dragon School with butterflies in his tummy — tiny flaming butterflies. He could barely finish his toast. What if no one liked him? What if he accidentally sneezed fire on someone? What if he was the worst dragon there? His mum smoothed down his scales. "Just be yourself," she said. At school, Drake accidentally sneezed and scorched the edge of a bench. He turned bright red with embarrassment. But the little dragon sitting next to him — a purple one named Pepper — just laughed kindly. "Mine went blue last week," Pepper said, "and melted a snow cone." They both giggled. By lunchtime they were sharing their sandwiches. By home time they were best friends. Drake flew home with no butterflies left, just a warm glow in his chest.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: The Kindness Tree
stories.description: Every act of kindness makes a magical tree grow a new golden leaf.
stories.content: In the centre of Willowbrook village stood a tree unlike any other. Its leaves were bright gold, but only when someone was kind. One morning little Rosa gave her sandwich to a boy who had forgotten his lunch — and a single golden leaf appeared on the tree. That afternoon old Mr Park helped a lost cat find its way home — two more leaves unfurled. A girl held an umbrella over a stranger in the rain. A boy helped his sister reach the high shelf. A grandmother left flowers on a neighbour's doorstep. With every kind act, another golden leaf shimmered into being. By evening the tree blazed like a lantern. People came from nearby streets to see it glow. "What makes it do that?" a small child asked. An old woman smiled. "The same thing that makes you feel warm inside when you are kind," she said.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

stories.title: The Little Explorer
stories.description: A toddler turns the backyard into a world of big discoveries.
stories.content: Every morning after breakfast, Nico put on his explorer hat — the one with the stripe — and went to explore the backyard. To Nico, the backyard was not small. It was enormous. Under the big pot near the fence lived a city of ants carrying crumbs bigger than their heads. Nico watched them for a long time. Behind the rosebush was a spiderweb that sparkled with dew drops, each one like a tiny planet. He found a feather that was striped brown and cream and wondered what bird it belonged to. He found a snail moving so slowly he had to wait a whole minute to see it move. At the end of the morning he sat on the back step and told his mum everything he had found. She listened to every single word. The backyard was exactly the right size for one small explorer with a big curious heart.
stories.author: BabyG Editorial Team

dailyUpdates.title: Newborn Care Tips
dailyUpdates.content: Newborns sleep 14-17 hours per day. Ensure safe sleep practices: place baby on back, firm mattress, no loose bedding.

dailyUpdates.title: Newborn Development
dailyUpdates.content: Your newborn can see 8-12 inches away. They respond to voices and prefer high-contrast patterns.

dailyUpdates.title: Safety Reminder
dailyUpdates.content: Always support baby's head and neck. Never shake a baby. Keep small objects out of reach.

dailyUpdates.title: Feeding Schedule
dailyUpdates.content: Most 1-month-olds feed every 2-3 hours. Watch for hunger cues like rooting or sucking motions.

dailyUpdates.title: Motor Development
dailyUpdates.content: Baby may start to lift head briefly during tummy time. This strengthens neck muscles.

dailyUpdates.title: Sleep Patterns
dailyUpdates.content: Babies this age may start sleeping longer at night. Establish a bedtime routine.

dailyUpdates.title: Social Development
dailyUpdates.content: Your baby may start smiling in response to your face. This is a major social milestone!

dailyUpdates.title: Activity Suggestion
dailyUpdates.content: Try reading board books with high-contrast images. Point to pictures and name objects.

dailyUpdates.title: Physical Milestones
dailyUpdates.content: Many babies can roll over by 4-6 months. Always supervise during tummy time.

dailyUpdates.title: Solid Food Introduction
dailyUpdates.content: Around 6 months, you can start introducing solid foods. Begin with single-ingredient purees.

dailyUpdates.title: Sitting Up
dailyUpdates.content: Most babies can sit without support by 8 months. Provide safe spaces for practice.

dailyUpdates.title: Crawling Activities
dailyUpdates.content: Encourage crawling with toys just out of reach. This builds strength and coordination.

dailyUpdates.title: Language Development
dailyUpdates.content: Babies may say first words around 10-12 months. Talk to your baby frequently.

dailyUpdates.title: Toddler Nutrition
dailyUpdates.content: Offer a variety of healthy foods. Let your toddler explore textures and flavors.

dailyUpdates.title: Walking Milestone
dailyUpdates.content: Most toddlers walk independently by 15-18 months. Provide safe spaces for practice.

dailyUpdates.title: Pretend Play
dailyUpdates.content: Encourage imaginative play with dolls, toy kitchen, or vehicles. This develops creativity.

sleepGuides.title: Newborn Sleep Guide (0-3 months)
sleepGuides.description: Understanding newborn sleep patterns and establishing healthy habits.
sleepGuides.overview: Newborns sleep 14-17 hours per day in 2-4 hour stretches. They cannot distinguish day from night yet.
tips: Sleep when baby sleeps to avoid exhaustion
Create a safe sleep environment — firm mattress, no loose bedding
Swaddling can help soothe newborns
Expose baby to natural light during daytime feeds
Keep nighttime interactions calm and quiet

sleepGuides.title: Infant Sleep Guide (4-6 months)
sleepGuides.description: Introducing sleep schedules and beginning sleep training if desired.
sleepGuides.overview: Babies at this age can begin to sleep for longer stretches and may be ready for gentle sleep training.
tips: Establish a consistent bedtime routine
Watch for sleep cues — yawning, rubbing eyes, fussiness
Try putting baby down drowsy but awake
Aim for an earlier bedtime (6:30-7:30 PM)
Begin consolidating naps into 3 per day

sleepGuides.title: Older Baby Sleep Guide (7-12 months)
sleepGuides.description: Transitioning to 2 naps and maintaining healthy sleep habits.
sleepGuides.overview: Most babies transition from 3 to 2 naps between 6-8 months and may sleep 10-12 hours overnight.
tips: Maintain a consistent sleep schedule on weekends too
Create a calming bedtime routine lasting 20-30 minutes
Ensure adequate daytime sleep to avoid overtiredness
Transition to 2 naps when baby consistently resists the third nap
Keep the sleep environment dark and cool

sleepGuides.title: Toddler Sleep Guide (12-24 months)
sleepGuides.description: Managing the transition to one nap and toddler sleep challenges.
sleepGuides.overview: Toddlers need 11-14 hours of sleep. Most transition to one nap between 15-18 months.
tips: Keep bedtime routine consistent and predictable
Limit screen time for at least 1 hour before bed
Use a white noise machine to block household sounds
Offer a comfort object like a stuffed animal
Watch for signs of nap readiness to drop

feedingGuides.title: Newborn Feeding Guide (0-4 months)
feedingGuides.description: Establishing breastfeeding or formula feeding with a newborn.
feedingGuides.overview: Newborns have small stomachs and need to feed frequently. Breast milk or formula provides complete nutrition.
tips: Feed on demand — typically every 2-3 hours
Look for hunger cues: rooting, sucking on hands, crying is a late cue
Ensure a good latch for breastfeeding
Burp baby during and after each feeding
Track wet diapers as a sign of adequate intake (6+ per day)

schedule_recommendations.amount_per_feeding: 60-90 ml formula or feed until satisfied at breast

adequacy_assessment_questions.question: Does baby have 6+ wet diapers per day?
Does baby seem satisfied after feeding?
adequacy_assessment_questions.good_sign: Yes — not constantly crying from hunger

feedingGuides.title: Starting Solids Guide (4-6 months)
feedingGuides.description: Introducing first foods alongside breast milk or formula.
feedingGuides.overview: Around 4-6 months, babies may show signs of readiness for solids. Breast milk or formula remains the primary nutrition source.
tips: Watch for readiness signs: head control, interest in food, doubled birth weight
Start with single-ingredient purees
Introduce one new food at a time, waiting 3-5 days before next
Never add salt, sugar, or honey to baby food
Continue breast milk or formula as primary nutrition

food_introduction_timeline.notes: Mix with breast milk or formula

adequacy_assessment_questions.question: Is baby still getting breast milk or formula?
Is baby accepting a variety of foods?

feedingGuides.title: Growing Appetite Guide (6-9 months)
feedingGuides.description: Expanding texture and variety as baby develops eating skills.
feedingGuides.overview: Babies at this stage can handle lumpier textures and a wider variety of flavors. Two solid meals per day are typical.
tips: Offer a variety of vegetables, fruits, and proteins
Gradually increase texture from smooth to mashed
Let baby explore self-feeding with soft finger foods
Offer water in a sippy cup with meals
Allow baby to set the pace — never force feeding

schedule_recommendations.amount_per_feeding: 120-150 ml formula + 2-3 tbsp solids per meal

adequacy_assessment_questions.question: Is baby eating 2 solid meals per day?
adequacy_assessment_questions.good_sign: Yes — good for this age range

feedingGuides.title: Finger Foods and Family Meals (9-12 months)
feedingGuides.description: Transitioning to three meals and joining family mealtimes.
feedingGuides.overview: Babies are ready for small soft finger foods and can begin to join family mealtimes with modified portions.
tips: Offer soft finger foods like banana slices, cooked pasta, soft cheese
Transition to 3 meals per day with 1-2 snacks
Let baby try to self-feed with a spoon
Offer a wide variety to prevent picky eating
Avoid choking hazards: whole grapes, raw carrots, nuts

adequacy_assessment_questions.question: Is baby eating a variety of foods from all food groups?
Is baby able to self-feed some foods?
Is baby drinking water with meals?
